In [[mathematics]], a '''monoidal adjunction''' is an adjunction between [[monoidal category|monoidal categories]] which respects their monoidal structures.<ref name="m560">{{cite web | title=monoidal adjunction | url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/monoidal+adjunction |publisher=nlab | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref><ref name="k469">{{cite journal | last=Lindner | first=Harald | title=Adjunctions in monoidal categories | journal=Manuscripta Mathematica | volume=26 | issue=1-2 | date=1978 | issn=0025-2611 | doi=10.1007/BF01167969 | pages=123–139}}</ref><ref name="k058">{{cite book | last=Hasegawa | first=Masahito | title=Models of Sharing Graphs | publisher=Springer Science & Business Media | publication-place=London | date=2012-12-06 | isbn=978-1-4471-0865-8 | page=64}}</ref>

Suppose that <math>(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)</math> and <math>(\mathcal D,\bullet,J)</math> are two [[monoidal category|monoidal categories]]. A '''monoidal adjunction''' between two [[lax monoidal functor]]s
:<math>(F,m):(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)\to (\mathcal D,\bullet,J)</math> and <math>(G,n):(\mathcal D,\bullet,J)\to(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)</math>
is an [[Adjoint functors|adjunction]] <math>(F,G,\eta,\varepsilon)</math> between the underlying functors, such that the [[natural transformation]]s
:<math>\eta:1_{\mathcal C}\Rightarrow G\circ F</math> and <math>\varepsilon:F\circ G\Rightarrow 1_{\mathcal D}</math>
are [[monoidal natural transformation]]s.

== Lifting adjunctions to monoidal adjunctions ==
Suppose that
:<math>(F,m):(\mathcal C,\otimes,I)\to (\mathcal D,\bullet,J)</math>
is a lax monoidal functor such that the underlying functor <math>F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D</math> has a right adjoint <math>G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C</math>. This adjunction lifts to a monoidal adjunction <math>(F,m)</math>⊣<math>(G,n)</math> if and only if the lax monoidal functor <math>(F,m)</math> is strong.

== See also ==
* Every monoidal adjunction <math>(F,m)</math>⊣<math>(G,n)</math> defines a [[monoidal monad]] <math>G\circ F</math>.
